name: Maghan II
summary:
Maghan II, or Kita Tenin Maghan, was a mansa of the Mali Empire from 1387 to 1389. Born into the royal family of the empire, he succeeded his father Mansa Mari Diata II as the ruler of the Mali Empire in 1387. During his reign, Maghan II focused on strengthening the empire's economy and trade relationships with neighboring regions.

The core events during Maghan II's rule were marked by significant military campaigns against rival empires, including the Songhai Empire. These campaigns resulted in the expansion of the Mali Empire's territory and influence in the region.

Maghan II's legacy can be seen in the continued prosperity of the Mali Empire under his successors, who maintained the empire's economic and cultural achievements. The empire's capital city, Niani, became a major center of trade and commerce during this period.

Despite his significant contributions to the Mali Empire, Maghan II's life was cut short when he died in 1389 at the age of unknown.

Maghan II's impact on West African history is evident in the continued growth and influence of the Mali Empire under subsequent rulers. His military campaigns helped establish the empire as a major power in the region, shaping the course of West African politics and culture for centuries to come.
